name: When do I need framing adjustments during a bathroom or kitchen renovation?

mainEntity.name: When do I need framing adjustments during a bathroom or kitchen renovation?

acceptedAnswer.text: You generally need framing adjustments whenever you change layout configurations, alter door sizes, or install recessed elements during a remodel. For instance, updating a bathroom may require framing a recessed medicine cabinet or shower shampoo niche between existing studs. In kitchens, removing an upper cabinet peninsula might call for cutting down a partition wall to counter height. If you want wider doorways for accessibility, converting standard 28-inch frames to 32- or 36-inch openings requires reframing the rough opening before hanging a new pre-hung door.
acceptedAnswer.description: You need framing adjustments when widening doorways, adding shower niches, shifting closet layouts, or trimming partition walls to fit new cabinetry and appliances.
